acalanthis.definition: acalanthis idis, f, a small bird, the gold-finch, thistle-finch, V.

accenseo.definition: accēnseō —, cēnsus, ēre, to reckon to, count among (rare): accenseor illi, am reckoned one of her attendants, O.

acceptio.definition: acceptiō ōnis, f accipio, a taking, receiving, accepting: frumenti, S.: donatio sine acceptione.

accessus.definition: accessus ūs, m accedo, a coming near, approach: ad urbem nocturnus: ad urbem accessus hominum multitudine florebat, i. e. was escorted by: ventorum, V. — Meton., a way of approach, passage, entrance: omnem accessum lu…

accingo.definition: accingō nxī, nctus, ere, to gird to, gird on, bind on, put on with a girdle, gird round: lateri ensem, V.; pass: accingitur ense, girds himself, V.: quo (ense) fuit accinctus, O.—Meton., to arm, equip, furnish, provid…

accio.definition: acciō (ad-c-) cīvī, cītus, īre, to call, summon, send for, invite: si accierit, accurram: Aenean acciri omnes Exposcunt, V.: ex Latio fortissimum quemque, S.: acciti ibant, they went at the summons, S.: in regnum Roma…

accipio.definition: accipiō cēpī, ceptus, ere ad+capio, to take without effort, receive, get, accept. — Of voluntary taking, to take, accept, take into possession, receive: obsides, Cs.: divitias, N.: aliquid a patre, inherit, N.: suspit…

acclamatio.definition: acclāmātiō (ad-c-) ōnis, f acclamo, a calling, shout, exclamation: acclamatione impediri: adversa populi: adclamationes multitudinis, L.

acclamo.definition: acclāmō (ad-c-) āvī, ātus, āre, to call to, shout at, exclaim: hostis omnibus, qui acclamassent: populus cum risu acclamavit, ipsa esse: (provincia) cui acclamari solet: ne acclametur times? cunctis servatorem liberat…

acclino.definition: acclīnō (ad-c-) āvī, ātus, āre CLI-, to cause to lean on, stay upon: se in illum, O.: castra tumulo sunt acclinata, L.— Fig., with se: haud gravate se ad causam senatūs, inclined, L.

acclivis.definition: acclīvis (ad-c-) e (once acclīvus, O.), adj. CLI-, up-hill, ascending, steep: leniter adclivis aditus, Cs.: trames, O.: tumulis adclive solum, sloping in knolls, V.

acclivitas.definition: acclīvitās ātis, f acclivis, an ascent, rising grade, acclivity: pari acclivitate collis, Cs.

accola.definition: 'accola ae, m COL-, he who dwells near, a neighbor: pastor, accola eius loci, L.: Cereris (i. e. her temple): Tiberis accolis fluviis orbatus, tributaries, Ta.'

accolo.definition: accolō (ad-c-) coluī, —, ere, to dwell near, be a neighbor to: illum locum: fluvium: saxum, V.

accommodatio.definition: accommodātiō (adc-) ōnis, f accommodo, an adjustment, accommodation: sententiarum ad inventionem. — Complaisance, regard: magistratuum.

accommodo.definition: accommodō (ad-c-) āvī, ātus, āre, to fit, adapt, put on, apply: coronam sibi ad caput: lateri ensem, V.: insignia, Cs.—Fig., to adjust, adapt, make fit for, accommodate: puppīs ad magnitudinem fluctuum, Cs.: oratio mu…

accommodus.definition: 'accommodus (ad-c-) adj., fit for, suitable for: valles fraudi, V.'

accredo.definition: accrēdō (ad-c-) crēdidī, —, ere, 3, to accord belief, believe fully: tibi nos adcredere par est, H. —Absol: vix adcredens.

accresco.definition: accrēscō (ad-c-) crēvī, crētus, ere, to grow progressively, increase, become greater: flumen subito: amicitia cum aetate adcrevit, T.: invidia, H. — Meton., to come gradually into being, arise, grow up: dictis factisq…

accubitio.definition: accubitiō ōnis, f accubo, a lying, reclining (at meals): epularis amicorum; absol: accubitio.

accumbo.definition: accumbō (ad-c-) cubuī, cubitum, ere CVB-, to lay oneself down, lie beside: mecum, T.: cum suis, N.—Esp., to recline at table: in convivio: in epulo: epulis divūm, V.; absol: ut vir adcumberet nemo.

accumulate.definition: accumulātē (ad-c-) adv. with sup. accumulo, abundantly, copiously: alqd facere: accumulatissime largiri, Her.

accumulator.definition: accumulator (ad-c-) ōris, m one who heaps up: opum, Ta.

accumulo.definition: accumulō (ad-c-) āvī, ātus, āre, to heap up, increase by heaping, amass: auget, addit, accumulat (pecuniam).—Fig., to add, increase, multiply: curas, O. — To confer abundantly: alcui summum honorem, O.: quibus non sua…

accuratio.definition: accūrātiō ōnis, f accuro, exactness, carefulness (once): in inveniendis rebus mira.

accuro.definition: accūrō (ad-c-) āvī, ātus, āre, to give close attention to, be careful: alqd, S.; with ne, T.

accurro.definition: accurrō (ad-c-) currī or cucurrī, cursus, ere, to run to, hasten to: ad praetorem: Marius adcurrit auxilio suis, to help, S.: accurrunt ad tempus tutores.—Fig., of ideas, present themselves, arise, C.

accursus.definition: accursus (ad-c-) ūs, m a running to, coming to: Remi, O.: tot provinciarum, Ta.

accusabilis.definition: accūsābilis (ad-c-) e, adj. accuso, that may be prosecuted, criminal: turpitudo (once).

accusator.definition: accūsātor ōris, m accuso, the accuser, prosecutor, plaintiff: acres atque acerbi: sui capitis, L.—Meton., an accuser, betrayer: suus, N.

accusatorius.definition: accūsātōrius adj. accusator, of a prosecutor, relating to a prosecution, making a complaint: lex: animus: spiritus, L.

acerbitas.definition: acerbitās ātis, f acerbus, bitterness, harshness, sourness: fructūs magnā acerbitate permixtos ferre, i. e. public rewards bringing also bitter trials. — Fig., harshness, bitterness, rigor, severity, hostility, hatred…

acerbo.definition: acerbō —, āre acerbus, to aggravate, make worse (rare): formidine crimen, V.

acernus.definition: 'acernus adj. 1 acer, of maple wood: trabes, V.: mensa, H.: solium, V.'

acervo.definition: acervō āvī, —, āre acervus, to heap up, pile up: cumulos hominum, L.—Fig., to multiply: leges, L.

acriculus.definition: ācriculus adj. dim. 2 ācer, irritable: senex.

additamentum.definition: additāmentum ī, n addo, an accession: inimicorum meorum, i. e. reinforcement.

adeptio.definition: adeptiō ōnis, f adipiscor, an obtaining, attainment: boni; alicuius commodi.

adequito.definition: ad - equitō āvī, —, āre, to ride to, gallop to, ride up: ad nostros, Cs.: in primos ordines, Cu.: quo, L.: portis, L.: ab suis, L.

adhinnio.definition: ad-hinniō īvī, —, īre, to neigh to, whinny to: equo, O.—Fig.: ad orationem, i. e. expressed delight.

adhortatio.definition: adhortātiō ōnis, f adhortor, an encouragement, exhortation: nostra: clamore conprobata, L.: invicem, L.: mutua, Cu.—Plur., L.

adhortator.definition: adhortātor ōris, m adhortor, one who encourages: operis, to the work, L.

admaturo.definition: ad-mātūrō —, —, āre, to mature (once): seditionem, Cs.

admetior.definition: ad-mētior mēnsus, īrī, dep., to measure out: tibi frumentum.

adminiculo.definition: adminiculō āre adminiculum, to prop: vitem (once).

administra.definition: ad-ministra ae, f administer, a female assistant, handmaid.—Fig.: artes administrae virtutis.

administrator.definition: administrātor ōris, m administro, a manager, conductor: belli gerendi.

agglutino.definition: agglutinō (ad-g-) —, —, āre, to glue to, stick on, fig.: prooemium.

aggravo.definition: aggravō (ad-g-) —, ātus, āre, to make heavy. — Fig., to embarrass further, increase in oppressiveness: res, L.: dolorem, Cu.: curam curā, Ph.

aggredior.definition: aggredior (ad-g-) gressus, ī, dep. ad + gradior, to approach: aliquo. — Esp., to approach, apply to, address: legatos aggreditur, S.: iudicem, to influence: mortales pecuniā, with bribes, S.: Venerem dictis, to accost…

aggressio.definition: aggressiō (adg-) ōnis, f aggredior, an assault; fig.: prima, the introduction (to a speech).

agilis.definition: 'agilis e, adj. 1 AG-, nimble, quick, agile, lively, prompt: Cyllenius, O.: agilis fio, a business man, H.: Quae circumvolitas agilis thyma? H.: remus, O.: rota, O.'

agilitas.definition: agilitās ātis, f agilis, nimbleness, activity, quickness: navium, L.: rotarum, Cu.—Fig.: naturae, a pliable temper.

agitabilis.definition: agitābilis e, adj. agito, easily moved, light: aer, O.

agitatio.definition: agitātiō ōnis, f agito, movement, motion, agitation: fluctuum: lecticae, L.: linguae: armorum, L. — Fig.: mentis. — Pursuit, prosecution: studiorum: magnarum rerum.

agitator.definition: agitātor ōris, m agito, a driver: aselli, V.: equorum Achillis, i. e. charioteer, V.—Esp., a competitor in the circus, C.

agito.definition: agitō āvī, ātus, āre, freq. ago, to set in violent motion, drive onward, move, impel, urge: (Harena) magnā vi agitata, S.: greges, drive to pasture, V.: equum, V.: iugales (dracones), O.: (triremem) in portu agitari i…

agmen.definition: āgmen inis, n ago, that which is driven.— In gen., a multitude, throng, host, troop, crowd, number, band: perpetuum totius Italiae: ingens mulierum, L.: puerile, of boys, V.: Eumenidum agmina, V.: navium, a line of sh…

agna.definition: āgna ae, f agnus, a ewe lamb, H., V., O.

agnascor.definition: āgnāscor (ad-gn-) ātus, to be born in addition (i. e. after a father's will was made): constat agnascendo rumpi testamentum; see agnatus.

agnatio.definition: āgnātiō (adg-) ōnis, f agnascor, consanguinity on the father's side: iura agnationum.

agnina.definition: āgnīna ae, f agnus, the flesh of a lamb, lamb, H.

agnitio.definition: āgnitiō ōnis, f agnosco, a knowing, knowledge: animi.

agnosco.definition: āgnōscō (ad-gn- or ad-n-) nōvī, nitus, ere, to recognize, identify, make out: illa reminiscendo: nomine audito virum, L.: veterem amicum, V.: non agnoscendum os, O.: hominem, Ph.: Augusti laudes, praise appropriate to…

agnus.definition: āgnus ī, m a lamb: villa abundat haedo agno: ara avet spargier agno, H., V., O.

ago.definition: agō ēgī, āctus (old inf pass. agier), ere 1 AG-, to put in motion, move, lead, drive, tend, conduct: bos Romam acta, L.: capellas, V.: pecus visere montīs, H.: ante se Thyum, N.: in exsilium, L.: Iris nubibus acta, bo…

agonium.definition: agōnium ī, n a victim, beast for sacrifice, O. —Plur. for Agonalia (see Agonalis), O.

agrarii.definition: agrāriī ōrum, m the agrarian party, supporters of agrarian laws, C., L.—

agrarius.definition: agrārius adj. ager, pertaining to land: lex, a law for the division of land, C., L.: largitio, a gratuitous land-grant, L.: agrariam rem tentare, to agitate for a distribution of land by law.—As subst:

agricola.definition: agricola ae, m ager + COL-, a husbandman, agriculturist, ploughman, farmer, peasant: adsidui: diligentissimus: fortunati, V.—Praegn., a rustic, boor, clown, C.—Poet.: caelitis, rustic deities, Tb.

agripeta.definition: agripeta ae, m ager + PET-, a colonist, one who seeks land to cultivate, C. (twice).

ah.definition: āh or ā interj.—Of distress or pity, ah! alas! H.—Of reproach or admonition, ah! oh! V.—Of surprise, Oh! I see! H.

ai.definition: ai ai)/, interj, alas, only O. (once).

aio.definition: āiō v. defect. for * ag-io, AG-; in use, praes. ind. āiō , aïs, aït, āiunt; subj. āias, āiat; imperf. āiē bam throughout, colloq., aibam (disyl.); part. āiēns (C. twice), to say yes, assent, affirm: negat quis? nego: …

ala.definition: āla ae, f for * axla; dim. of axis, a wing: aquila suspensis demissa leniter alis, L.: stridentes, V. — Fig.: mors alis circumvolat atris, H.: furva, Tb.: iocunda, Pr.: fulminis ocior alis, V.: timor addidit alas, i. …

alacer.definition: alacer (m alacris, T., V.), cris, cre, adj. with comp. AL-, lively, brisk, quick, eager, excited, glad, happy: quidve es alacris? why so excited? T.: videbant Catilinam alacrem atque laetum, active and joyous: ex alac…

alacritas.definition: alacritās ātis, f alacer, liveliness, ardor, eagerness, alacrity, cheerfulness, encouragement: quantam mihi alacritatem ... concursus adferret: alacritate ac studio uti, Cs.: ingens, Ta.: animi, Cs.: rei p. defendenda…

alapa.definition: alapa ae, f a box on the ear, blow with the open hand: alapam sibi ducere, Ph.: ridere Mamercorum alapas, mock slaps (on the stage), Iu.— Given in the ceremony of emancipation, hence: multo maioris alapae mecum veneun…

alarius.definition: ālārius adj. ala, of the wing (of an army): cohortes, Cs.: equites, L., Ta. — Plur. as subst, auxiliary troops: ad speciem alariis uti, Cs.

alatus.definition: ālātus adj. ala, winged, having wings (poet.): plantae (of Mercury), V.: equi, O.

albatus.definition: albātus adj. albus, white - robed, clothed in white: epuli dominus: natalis (dies), H.

albeo.definition: albeō —, —, ēre albus, to be white: campi ossibus, V., O.: albente caelo, at dawn, Cs.

albesco.definition: albēscō —, —, ere, inch, to become white, whiten: mare albescit: fluctus vento, V.: albescens capillus, H.: flammarum tractus, brightens, V.: lux, dawns, V.

albico.definition: albicō —, —, āre albus, to be white: prata pruinis, H.: albicans litus, Ct.

albidus.definition: 'albidus adj. albus, whitish, white: spuma, O.'

albulus.definition: 'albulus adj. dim. albus, whitish: columbus, Ct.'

album.definition: album ī, n albus, white color, whiteness: insignis albo, V.: columnas polire albo, L. — Meton., a white tablet on which the Pontifex Maximus registered the principal events of the year (cf. Annales maximi): in album r…

albus.definition: albus adj., white (without lustre, opp. ater; cf. candidus, opp. niger): color: hedera, V.: plumbum, i. e. tin, Cs.: parma, i. e. unadorned, V.: canities, O.: vitis, bryony, O.: pallor, ghastly, H.: lapis, marble, H.:…

alces.definition: alcēs is, f the elk, Cs.

alea.definition: alea ae, f a game with dice: in aleā tempus consumere: exercere aleam, Ta.: luditur pernox, Iu.—Chance, hazard, risk, fortune, venture: dubia imperii servitiique, L.: dare in aleam tanti casūs se regnumque, set at ris…

aleator.definition: āleātor ōris, m alea, a player with dice, gamester.

aleatorius.definition: āleātōrius adj. aleator, of a gamester: damna, in gaming.

aleo.definition: āleō ōnis, m a gamester, Ct.

alga.definition: alga ae, f sea-weed, H.—Prov. of worthlessness: proiecta, V.: inutilis, H.

algor.definition: algor ōris, m algeo, cold, chilliness: corpus patiens algoris, S.

alias.definition: aliās adv. orig. acc plur. f. of alius, of time, at another time, some other time, at other times: Nil oriturum alias, nil ortum tale fatentes, H.: et alias et in consulatūs petitione vincebar: numquam ante alias, L.:…

alibi.definition: alibī adv., elsewhere, somewhere else, at another place (cf. alio loco): Catulo alibi reponamus, find another place for: alibi servaturi auferuntur, Ta. —Esp., alibi ... alibi, in one place ... in another; here ... th…

alicubi.definition: alicubī adv. old aliquōbī, at any place, somewhere, anywhere: utinam hic prope adsit alicubi, T.: hic alicubi in Crustumenio.

alicunde.definition: alicunde adv. ali- + cunde (unde), from somewhere, from any place: venire, T.: decedere. —Meton.: non quaesivit procul alicunde, from any other source: alicunde sumere, from somebody, T.: alicunde obiectus labor, from…

alienatio.definition: aliēnātiō ōnis, f alieno, of property, a transfer, surrender: sacrorum, i. e. a transfer of the sacred rites to another gens.— Fig., a separation, alienation, breach: consulum: patrui, Ta.: amicitiae: tua a me.—Desert…

alieno.definition: aliēnō āvī, ātus, āre alienus, to make strange, make another's, transfer, make over, part with: de vectigalibus alienandis: a vobis alienari (sc. res): parvo pretio ea.—To make subject to another, give up, lose: urbs …

aliger.definition: āliger gera, gerum, adj. ala + GES-, bearing wings, winged: amor, V.: agmen, i. e. of birds, V.

alimentarius.definition: alimentārius adj., pertaining to nourishment lex, for distributing food among the poor, Cael. ap. C.

alimentum.definition: alimentum ī, n alo, nourishment, nutriment, aliment: corporis: alimentum famae, Ta.—Plur, food, provisions<*> miseranda, Ta.: flammae, fuel, O.: lacrimae ei alimenta fuere, tears were his food, O.—The return due to pa…

alimonium.definition: alimōnium ī, n nourishment, sustenance, Ta.

alioqui.definition: aliōquī (less correctly aliōquīn), adv., in another way, in other respects, for the rest, otherwise: alioqui acceptam dis hostiam esse, L.: vitiis paucis Mendosa natura, alioqui recta, H.: triumphatum de Tiburtibus, a…

aliorsum.definition: aliōrsum adv. contr. for alio-vorsum, in another direction, in another manner, in a different sense: aliorsum atque ego feci, T.

aliptes.definition: alīptēs or alīpta ae, m, a)lei/pths, one who anointed wrestlers, a wrestling-master, C., Iu.

aliqua.definition: aliquā adv., by any way, in any direction, any whither: aliquā evolare: evadere, L. — In some way, somehow: id aliquā resciscere, T.: nocere, V.

aliquantus.definition: 'aliquantus adj., of an indefinite quantity, some, considerable, moderate: signorum numerus, S.: timor aliquantus, sed spes amplior, S.: spatium, L.'

aliqui.definition: aliquī aliqua, aliquod, gen. alicūius, dat. and abl plur. aliquī s or aliquibus, pronom adj. indef. ali- + qui, some, any: si est aliqui sensus in morte praeclarorum virorum: evadit in aliquod magnum malum, T.: signif…

aliquis.definition: aliquis aliqua, aliquid, nom. and acc plur. neut. aliqua, dat. aliquī s or aliquibus, pron indef., some one, any one, anybody, one or another; neut., something, anything. I. As pron. subst: Quom ex te esset aliquis, q…

aliquot.definition: 'aliquot indef. num. indecl. , some, several, a few, not many, a number: dies, T.: aliquot abacorum: aliquot de causis, Cs.: aliquot me adierunt, T.: aliquot occidere, multos ferro, etc.'

aliter.definition: aliter adv. alis, in another manner, otherwise, in any other way, differently. — With atque, ac, quam or ut, otherwise than, different from what: sed aliter atque ostenderam facio: aliter ac nos vellemus: de quo tu al…

aliunde.definition: 'aliunde adv., from another, from another source, from elsewhere: adsumpto aliunde uti bono: non aliunde pendere: aliunde quam: Qui aliunde stet semper, aliunde sentiat, supports one party, sympathizes with the other,…

almus.definition: almus adj. 1 AL-, nourishing, fruitful, foodgiving (poet.): Ceres, V.: ager, V. — Fig., kind, propitious, bountiful, favorable: Fides, Enn. ap. C.: Venus, H.: adorea, H.

alnus.definition: alnus ī, f 1 AL-, the alder: crassis paludibus alni Nascuntur, V. — Poet., a boat (of alderwood): cavatae, V.: undam levis innatat alnus, V.

alo.definition: alō aluī, altus or alitus, ere 1 AL-, to feed, nourish, support, sustain, maintain: altus inter arma, L.: canes ad venandum, T.: exercitum: magnum numerum equitatūs, Cs.: quos lingua periurio alebat, S.: publice ali, …

aloe.definition: aloē ēs, f, a)lo/h, the aloe.—Fig., bitterness: plus aloes quam mellix, Iu.

altercatio.definition: altercātiō ōnis, f altercor, a debate, discussion, alternate discourse: Lentuli et Caninii: magnā de re cum Velleio: altercatione congredi, L.

alterco.definition: altercō āvī, —, āre, to wrangle: cum patre, T.

alterno.definition: alternō āvī, —, āre alternus, to do by turns, interchange: vices, to exchange parts, O.: alternanti potior sententia visa, hesitating, V.: alternantes proelia miscent, fight by turns, V.

alternus.definition: alternus adj. alter, one after the other, alternate, in turn, reciprocal: ex duabus orationibus capita alterna recitare: alternis trabibus ac saxis, beams alternating with stones, Cs.: pes, H.: alterni si congrediamur…

alteruter.definition: alter-uter utra, utrum, gen. alterutrīus (rarely separate, altera utra, etc.), pronom. adj., one or the other, either this or that, one of two: necesse erat alterutrum esse hostem: ut si in alterutro peccandum sit, ma…

alticinctus.definition: alticinctus adj. alte + cinctus, high-girded, i. e. active, busy, Ph.

altilis.definition: altilis is, adj. 1 AL-, fattened, fat.—As subst f., a fattened bird: satur altilium, H.: anseribus par, Iu.

altisonus.definition: 'altisonus adj. alte + sonus, of lofty sound: Iuppiter: Maro, Iu.'

altitudo.definition: altitūdō dinis, f altus, height, altitude: aedium: montium: muri, N.: altitudines, heights, L.: in altitudinem pedum LXXX, Cs.—Meton., depth: spelunca infinitā altitudine: maris, Cs.— Fig., height, elevation, loftines…

altor.definition: altor ōris, m alo, a nourisher, sustainer, foster-father: omnium rerum: altore recepto, O.

altrix.definition: altrīx īcis, f altor, a foster-mother, cherisher, sustainer: eorum terra altrix dicitur: Ulixi, V.: altricis limen Apuliae, H.—A wet-nurse, O.

altus.definition: altus adj. with comp. and sup. P. of alo, nourished, grown great, high, lofty, tall: altior illis, taller, O.: montes, V.—Meton., deep: altissimae radices: altissima flumina, Cs.: altior aqua, Cs.: volnus, V.—Fig., hi…

alucinor.definition: ālūcinor (not hālūcinor, hallū-), ātus, ā rī, dep., to wander in mind, talk unreasonably, ramble in thought: suspicor hunc alucinari: epistulae nostrae debent interdum alucinari, indulge in vague digressions: quae alu…

alumna.definition: 'alumna ae, f alo, a foster-daughter, pupil: aquai dulcis alumnae (of frogs): civitatis quasi alumna eloquentia.'

alumnus.definition: alumnus ī, m alo, a foster-son, ward, nursling: Carus, V.: dulcis, H.: hos usūs praestet tibi alumnus, i. e. this will be your reward for bringing him up, O.: legionum, brought up in the camp, Ta.: eorum agrorum alumn…

aluta.definition: alūta ae, f a soft leather prepared with alum: alutae tenuiter confectae, Cs.—Meton., a shoe latchet: nivea, O.: nigra, Iu. — A purse, pouch: tumidā superbus alutā, Iu.—A patch on the face, O.

alveolus.definition: alveolus ī, m dim. alveus, a tray, trough, basin: ligneus, Ph., L., Ta.—An oil jar, Iu.—A dice-board, C.—The bed of a small river, Cu.

alvus.definition: alvus ī, f AL-, the belly, paunch, bowels, womb: purgatio alvi: spem in alvo continere: matris, H.: in suam sua viscera congerit alvum, stomach, O.— The hold (of a ship), Ta.

amabilis.definition: amābilis e, adj. with comp. and sup. amo, worthy of love, lovely, amiable, attractive: filiola tua: insania, H.: frigus, refreshing, H.: carmen, a pleasant song: amabilior Velia: amabilissimus modus amicitiae.

amandatio.definition: āmandātiō ōnis, f amando, a sending away.

amando.definition: ā-mandō āvī, ātus, āre, to send away, remove: eum in ultimas terras: hominem quo?

amanter.definition: 'amanter adv. with comp. and sup. amans, lovingly, affectionately, amiably: meum adventum videre: amantius (facere), Ta.: quocum amantissime vixerat.'

amaracus.definition: amāracus ī, f, a)ma/rakos, marjoram: mollis, V.: Suave olens, Ct.

amarantus.definition: amarantus ī, n, a)ma/rantos, the amaranth, O., Tb.

amarities.definition: amāritiēs —, acc. em, f bitterness: dulcis, Ct.

amaror.definition: amāror ōris, m amarus, bitterness (poet.), V.

amarus.definition: amārus adj. with comp, bitter, pungent: salices, V.: calices amariores, Ct.: Doris, i. e. the brackish sea, V.—Fig., bitter, afflicting, sad: casū s, O.: amores dulces, V.—Plur n. as subst, bitternesses, bitter things…

amator.definition: amātor ōris, m amo, a lover, friend: noster: urbis, H.: antiquitatis, N.—A lover, one fond of women: adulter an amator: vinosus, amator, H.

amatorius.definition: amātōrius adj. amator, loving, amorous, amatory: voluptas: poë sis.

ambedo.definition: ambedō ēdī, ēsus ambi + 1 edo, to eat around, waste, consume: flammis ambesa Robora, V.: ambesae mensae, V.: quidquid, Ta.

ambiguitas.definition: ambiguitās ātis, f ambiguus, ambiguity, equivocalness, double sense: nominis: verbi, L.

ambiguus.definition: ambiguus adj. ambi + 1 AG-, going two ways, wavering, uncertain: per ambiguum favorem gratiam victoris spectare, by showing equal favor to both sides, L.: Proteus, assuming different forms, O.: Ambiguam tellure novā S…

ambitio.definition: ambitiō ōnis, f ambio, a going about.— Esp., of candidates for office, the soliciting of votes (by lawful means): mea me ambitio cogitatione abstrahebat: tanta exarsit ambitio, ut, etc., L.: Quid de nostris ambitionib…

ambitiosus.definition: ambitiōsus adj. with comp. ambitio, surrounding, encompassing, entwining: lascivis hederis ambitiosior, H.—Fig., ambitious, conciliatory, eager for honor, solicitous of favor: pro nato mater, O.: in Graecos: malis art…

ambo.definition: ambō ambae, ambō, acc m. ambō or ambōs, num. cf. ambi-, both (of a pair or couple): duae res ... quae ambae: (duo) senatores, qui ambo: ut eos ambos fallam, T.: ambo florentes aetatibus, Arcades ambo, V.: Se satis amb…

ambrosia.definition: ambrosia ae, f, a)mbrosi/a, ambrosia, sustenance of immortal life, food of the gods: ambrosiā deos laetari: orator ambrosiā alendus, i. e. divine.— Poet.: (equos) ambrosiae suco saturos, O.: ambrosiā Contigit os fecit…

ambrosius.definition: 'ambrosius adj., a)mbro/sios, divine, ambrosial: comae, V.'

ambubaia.definition: ambūbāia ae, f Syriac, a Syrian girl, fluteplayer and dancer: ambubaiarum collegia, H.

ambulatio.definition: ambulātiō ōnis, f ambulo, a walking about, walk: pomeridiana.— A walk, place for walking.

ambulatiuncula.definition: ambulātiuncula ae, dim, f. ambulatio, a short walk, little promenade.— A portico: tecta.

ambulo.definition: ambulō āvī, ātus, āre am- (for ambi) + BA-, to walk, walk about, take a walk: ambulando contrivi diem, T.: in sole: satis ambulatum est.—To go, travel, march: biduo septingenta milia passuum.—To traverse: maria: vias,…

amburo.definition: amb-ūrō ūssī, ūstus, ere ambi + uro, to burn round, scorch, singe, consume: hic (Verres) sociorum ambustus incendio: Terret ambustus Phaethon avaras Spes, H.—Jestingly: tribunus ambustus, singed: libris Ambustus propr…

amellus.definition: amellus ī, m purple Italian starwort, V.

amens.definition: ā-mēns entis, adj. with comp. and sup. ab + mens, out of one's senses, mad, frantic, distracted: arma amens capio, V.: homo amentissimus: metu, L.: magnitudine periculi, Cu.: animi, V.: malis cor, L.—Foolish, stupid: …

amentia.definition: āmentia ae, f amens, want of reason, madness, senselessness: Quor meam senectutem huius sollicito amentiā? T.: amentiā atque audaciā praeditus: tanta vis amentiae, L. — Folly: si quem amentia verset, H.

amentum.definition: āmentum ī, n a strap, thong: epistula ad amentum deligata, Cs.: amenta torquent, V.

ames.definition: 'ames itis, m 1 AP-, a fork for spreading nets: levis, H.'

amethystinus.definition: 'amethystinus adj., a)methu/stinos, of the amethyst, violet - colored: amythystina (sc. vestimenta), violet cloaks, Iu.'

amica.definition: amīca ae, f 1 amicus, a female friend, T., O., Iu.—A mistress, concubine, C., T.

amicitia.definition: amīcitia ae, f amicus, friendship: Per nostram amicitiam, T.: inter aliquos: esse in amicitiā cum aliquo, N.: iungere: parere, N.: dedere se amicitiae alicuius, Cs.: intima alicuius, N.: iura amicitiae: deficere ab am…

amicula.definition: amīcula ae, f dim. amica, a loved one, mistress: de amiculā rixatus.

amiculum.definition: amiculum ī, n amicio, an outer garment, mantle, cloak: amicae: purpureum, L.

amiculus.definition: amīculus ī, m dim. 2 amicus, a pet friend, crony: meus: quae censet amiculus, H.

amissio.definition: āmissiō ōnis, f amitto, a losing, loss: oppidorum: dignitatis: liberorum.

amita.definition: amita ae, f a father's sister, C., L., Ta.

amitto.definition: ā-mittō īsī (amīstī, for amīsisti, T.), issus, ere ab + mitto, to send away, dismiss, part with: abs te filium, T.— To let go, let slip: praedam ex oculis, L.: praedam de manibus: clavum, V.— Fig., to loose, let slip:…

amnicola.definition: 'amnicola ae, m and f amnis + COL-, that grows near a river: salices, O.'

amniculus.definition: amniculus ī, m dim. amnis, a rivulet, L.

amnis.definition: amnis is (abl. amne or amnī, V., H., L.), m 3 AC-, AP-, a river: Tiberinus, L.: si amnes exaruissent: navium patiens, L.: taciturnus, H.: secundo amni, down-stream, V.—Fig.: abundantissimus amnis artium.—Poet., a torr…

amoenitas.definition: amoenitās ātis, f amoenus, pleasantness, delightfulness: hortorum: cuius (domūs), N.: urbium, L.: vitae, Ta.—Plur: litorum.

amotio.definition: āmōtiō ōnis, f amoveo, a putting away.

amoveo.definition: ā-moveō ōvī, ōtus, ēre ab + moveo, to move away, take away, remove: testem abs te, T.: virgas a civium corpore: alia ab hostium oculis, L.: illum ex istis locis. — Esp., with pron reflex., to take oneself off, retire,…

amphitheatrum.definition: amphitheātrum ī, n, a)mfithe/atron, an amphitheatre, oval building for public spectacles, Ta.

amplector.definition: amplector exus, ī, dep. am- + plecto, to twine around, encircle, encompass, embrace: manibus saxa, to grasp, L.: ansas acantho, V.: urbes muro, H.: illam in somnis, T.: me: Nox tellurem amplectitur alis, overshadows, …

amplexor.definition: amplexor ātus, ārī, dep. intens. amplector, to embrace: mitto amplexari, T.: inimicum. — Fig., to be fond of, value, esteem: me: otium.

amplificatio.definition: amplificātiō ōnis, f amplifico, an extending, enlarging: pecuniae: rei familiaris.—Fig.: honoris.—In rhet., an ornate description, amplification.

amplificator.definition: amplificātor ōris, m amplifico, one who enlarges, a decorator, amplifier: rerum: dignitatis.

amplifico.definition: amplificō āvī, ātus, āre amplus + facio, to broaden, extend, enlarge, increase, make wide, give space to: urbem: urbs amplificanda, L.: divitias: vestris iudiciis amplificatam (auctoritatem): Aeduorum auctoritatem apu…

amplio.definition: ampliō āvī, ātus, āre amplus, to widen, extend, increase, enlarge, amplify: rem, H.: servitia, Ta.—In law, to delay a judgment, adjourn, reserve a decision (by the technical word amplius): causam: potestas ampliandi. …

amplitudo.definition: amplitūdō inis, f amplus, wide extent, width, amplitude, breadth, size, bulk: simulacrum modicā amplitudine: urbis, L.: soli, Ta.: amplitudines bonorum.—Fig., greatness: animi: rerum gestarum, N.—Dignity, grandeur, co…

amplus.definition: amplus adj. with comp. and sup. am- (for ambi-) + PLE-, of large extent, great, ample, spacious, roomy: domus, V.: civitas, Cs., C.: porticūs, V.: ter amplum Geryonem ... compescit, H.: amplum et excelsum signum, broa…

ampulla.definition: ampulla ae, f ambi + olla, a vessel for liquids, with two handles, a flask, bottle, jar.—Of inflated discourse, swelling words, bombast: proicit ampullas, H.

ampullor.definition: ampullor —, —, ārī, dep. ampulla, to talk bombast, H.

amputatio.definition: amputātiō ōnis, f amputo, a pruning, lopping off. sarmentorum.

amputo.definition: am - putō āvī, ātus, āre, to cut around, cut away, lop off, prune: vitem ferro: quicquid est pestiferum. — Fig., to curtail, shorten, diminish: amputata inanitas, removed.—In rhet.: amputata loqui, disconnectedly.

amurca.definition: amurca (amurga) ae, f, a)mo/rgh, the waste in pressing olives, dregs of oil, V.

amygdalum.definition: amygdalum ī, n, a)mu/gdalon, an almond, almond kernel, O.

amystis.definition: amystis idis, f, a)/mustis, the emptying of a cup at a draught, a bumper, H.

anagnostes.definition: anāgnōstēs ae, m, a)nagnw/sths, a reader, one who reads aloud (Lat. lector): noster.

anaticula.definition: anaticula ae, f dim. anas, a duckling.

anatocismus.definition: anatocismus ī, m, a)natokismo/s, interest upon interest, compound interest.

ancile.definition: ancīle is (gen plur. -ilium, Ta., once, -iliorum, H.), n a small oval shield, V.; usu. the shield said to have fallen from heaven in the reign of Numa, and on the preservation of which the prosperity of Rome was decla…

ancilla.definition: 'ancilla ae, f dim. ancula, a female attendant, a maid-servant, handmaid: aere empta, T.: ancillarum comitatus: mulier ancilla, S.'

ancillula.definition: ancillula ae, f dim. ancilla, a young female slave, handmaid: ex Aethiopiā , T.—Fig.: eloquentiae.

ancora.definition: ancora ae, f, a)/gkura, an anchor: dente Ancora fundabat naves, V.: ancoram iacere, to cast anchor, Cs.: tenere navem in ancoris, N.: ad ancoram constitit, lay at anchor, Cs.: tollere, to weigh anchor, Cs.: praecidere…

ancorale.definition: ancorāle is, n ancora, an anchor-cable: ancoralia incidunt, L.

ancorarius.definition: ancorārius adj. ancora, of an anchor: funes, cables, Cs.

andabata.definition: andabata ae, m a gladiator, who fought blindfold.

androgynus.definition: androgynus ī, m, a)ndro/gunos, a man woman, hermaphrodite.

anellus.definition: ānellus (ann-) ī, m dim. anulus, a little ring, H.

anethum.definition: anēthum ī, n, a)/nhthon, dill, anise: bene olens, V.

anfractus.definition: ānfrāctus ūs, m am- (for ambi-) + FRAG-, a recurving, turning, bending round: quae (figura) nihil incisum anfractibus habere potest: solis, a circuit.—Esp., a tortuous way, circuitous route: si nullus anfractus interc…

anguiculus.definition: anguiculus ī, m dim. anguis, a small serpent.

anguilla.definition: anguilla ae, f dim. anguis, an eel, Iu.

anguineus.definition: 'anguineus adj., of serpents, snaky: Gorgonis comae, O.'

anguinus.definition: anguīnus (trisyl.), adj. anguis, of serpents, snaky: capillus, Ct.

angustia.definition: angustia ae (sing. very rare), and angustiae, ārum, f angustus, narrowness, straitness: itineris, Cs.: loci, S. — Meton., a narrow place, narrow part, neck, defile, strait: Graeciae: angustiae saltibus inclusae, pass,…

angusto.definition: angustō —, —, āre angustus, to make narrow, straiten: iter corporum acervis, Ct.

angustus.definition: angustus adj. with comp. and sup. ANG-, narrow, strait, contracted: iter, S.: fines, Cs.: rima, H.: mare, a strait: angustissima portus, Cs.— Fig., short, brief: dies, O.: spiritus, breathing.— Needy, pinching, stinti…

anhelitus.definition: anhēlitus ūs, m anhelo, a difficulty of breathing, panting, puffing, deep breathing: a lasso ore, O.: vini, drunken reviling: sublimis, H.: aeger, V.—Meton., an exhalation, vapor: terrae.

anicula.definition: 'anicula ae, f dim. anus, a little old woman, granny, T.: minime suspiciosa.'

animadversor.definition: animadversor ōris, m animadverto, a censor (once): vitiorum.

anteeo.definition: ante-eō īvī or iī, —, īre (anteit, disyl., H., O.; anteirent, trisyl., V.; anteat, O.; antībō, Ta.; antissent, Ta.; antisse, Ta.), to go before, precede: strenuus anteis, H.: ubi anteire primores vident, L.: Te semper…

antefero.definition: ante-ferō tulī, lātum, ferre, to bear in front, carry before: quod fasces anteferrentur, Cs. — Fig., of estimation, to place before, prefer: alqd commodis suis: pacem bello: te Grais, H.

antefixus.definition: ante-fīxus adj. ante + figo, fastened before: truncis arborum antefixa ora, i. e. skulls, Ta. — Plur n. as subst, little images on the front of a house or temple, L.

antegredior.definition: antegredior essus, ī, dep. ante + gradior, to go before, precede: solem. — In time: cum antegressa est honestas: causae antegressae.

antehabeo.definition: ante-habeō —, —, ēre, to prefer: quieta turbidis, Ta.: incredibilia veris, Ta.

antehac.definition: ante-hāc (disyl., H.), adv. of time, before this time, before now, formerly, hitherto: fecit, T.: antehac uti solebat, etc.: antehac nefas (erat) ... dum, etc., H.—Before that time, earlier, previously: saepe antehac …

antelucanus.definition: antelūcānus adj. ante + lux, before light, before dawn: tempus: cenae, lasting all night.

antemeridianus.definition: ante-merīdiānus adj., before mid-day, of the forenoon: sermo: ambulatio.

antepilanus.definition: ante-pīlānus ī, m a soldier of the first two ranks, in front of the triarii, L.

antepono.definition: ante - pōnō posuī, positus, ere, to set before: propugnacula anteposita, Ta.: equitum locos sedilibus, Ta.—Fig., to prefer, value above: amicitiam omnibus rebus: gloria formulis anteponenda est: gloriam potentiae, S.—…

antes.definition: antēs īum, m rows (of vines), V.

antesignanus.definition: ante-sīgnānus ī, m ante + signum, a leader in battle: in acie.—Plur m. as subst., the soldiers who fought in front of the standards, Cs., L.

anthias.definition: anthias ae, m an unknown sea-fish, O.

anticipatio.definition: anticipātiō ōnis, f anticipo, a preconception, preconceived notion: deorum.

anticipo.definition: anticipō āvī, ātus, āre ante + CAP-, to take before, anticipate: rei molestiam: anticipata via est, travelled more quickly, O.

anticus.definition: antīcus adj. ANT-, in front, foremost: pars; see also antiquus.

antidotum.definition: antidotum ī, n, a)nti/doton, a remedy against poison, Ph.

antiquarius.definition: antiquarius ī, m an antiquarian, Ta., O.

antique.definition: antīquē adv. with comp. antiquus, like the ancients, in the old fashion: dicere, H.: antiquius permutatione mercium uti, the old method of barter, Ta.

antiquus.definition: antīquus (-īcus) adj. with comp. and sup. ante, ancient, former, of old times: tua duritia, former severity, T.: causa antiquior memoriā tuā : patria, L.: urbs, V.: antiquae leges et mortuae. —Plur m. as subst, the an…

anularius.definition: ānulārius ī, m anulus, a maker of rings.

anxietas.definition: ānxietās ātis, f anxius, anxiety, solicitude: animi, O.: perpetua, Iu.

anxitudo.definition: ānxitūdō dinis, f anxius, trouble, distress.

apeliotes.definition: apēliōtēs ae, m, a)phliw/ths, the east wind, Ct.

applicatio.definition: applicātiō (adp-) ōnis, f applico, an inclination: animi.— The relation of a client to his patron, clientship: ius applicationis.

approbator.definition: approbātor (adp-) ōris, m approbo, one who approves: profectionis.

approbo.definition: approbō (ad-p-) āvī, ātus, āre, to assent to, favor, approve:, id si non fama adprobat, T.: orationem, Cs.: falsa pro veris: approbatā sententiā: ita fieri oportere: dis approbantibus: illud clamore.—To make acceptabl…

appromitto.definition: apprōmittō (ad-p-) —, —, ere, to promise besides, join in a promise.

appropero.definition: approperō (ad-p-) āvī, ātus, āre.—Trans, to hasten, accelerate: opus, L.: intercisis venis mortem, Ta.: portas intrare, O.—Intrans, to hasten, make haste: ad facinus: approperate!

apricatio.definition: aprīcātiō ōnis, f apricor, a basking, sunning.

apricus.definition: aprīcus adj., exposed to the sun, warmed by sunshine, sunny: hortus: campus, H. — As subst: in apricum proferre, to bring to light, H.—Poet., delighting in sunshine: arbor, O.: mergi, V.: flores, H.

apto.definition: aptō āvī, ātus, āre aptus, to adapt, fit, apply, adjust: lacertos, V.: dexteris enses, H.: nervo sagittas, V.: habendo ensem, for wielding, V.— With abl: se armis, L.: ensem vaginā, V. — To accommodate, adapt: Nolis b…

aptus.definition: aptus P. and adj. P. of *apo; cf. apiscor. I. As part, fastened, joined, fitted, bound, attached: gladium e setā. — Fig., depending upon, arising from: causae aliae ex aliis aptae: ex verbis ius: vita apta virtute: ru…

aqua.definition: aqua ae (poet. also aquāī, V.), f 3 AC-, water: aquae pluviae, rain-water: gelida: pluvialis, O.: aquae fons: deterrima, most unwholesome, H.: perennis, L.: fervens, boiling: in aquam ruere, into the river, L.: aquae …

aquaticus.definition: aquāticus adj. aqua, growing in water, aquatic: lotos, O. — Bringing rain: Auster, O.

aquilonius.definition: aquilōnius adj. aquilo, northern, northerly: regio.

aquor.definition: aquor ātus, ārī, dep. aqua, to fetch water: aegre, Cs.: flumen, unde aquabantur, L.—Supin. acc.: miles aquatum egressus, S., L.—Of bees, V.

aquosus.definition: aquōsus adj. aqua, abounding in water, rainy, moist, watery: campus, L.: hiemps, rainy winter, V.: nubes, rain-clouds, O.: languor, i. e. dropsy, H.: Piscis, rainy, O.

ara.definition: āra ae, f AS-, a structure for sacrifice, altar: ex arā sume verbenas, T.: dicata, L. — Esp., of altars to the Penates, in the impluvia, while the Lares had a focus in the atrium; hence, arae et foci, hearth and home,…

arcula.definition: arcula ae, f dim. arca, a small box, casket: muliebres.—Fig., treasures (of language).

armilla.definition: 'armilla ae, f armus, a bracelet, armlet, armsing: aureae, L.'

armillatus.definition: armillātus adj. armilla, decked with bracelets: canes. Pr.

armisonus.definition: 'armisonus adj. arma + SON-, resounding with arms: Pallas, V.'

artopta.definition: artopta ae, f, a)rto/pths, a breadpan, Iu.

arula.definition: ārula ae, f dim. ara, a small altar.

arvina.definition: arvīna ae, f grease, fat, lard: pinguis, V.

averro.definition: āverrō —, —, ere ab + verro, to sweep away: carā piscīs mensā, i. e. to clear the (fishmonger's) table at a high price, H.

averrunco.definition: ā-verruncō —, —, āre, in religion, to avert: dii averruncent: averruncandae deum irae victimas caedere, for averting, L.: prodigia, L.

avia.definition: 'avia ae, f avus, a grandmother: anus, Cu.'

avitus.definition: avītus adj. avus, of a grandfather, ancestral: possessiones: nomen, O.: solium, V.: malum, hereditary, L.: nobilitas, Ta.

avocatio.definition: āvocātiō ōnis, f avoco, a diversion, distraction: a cogitandā molestiā.

avoco.definition: ā-vocō āvī, ātus, āre, to call off, call away: populum ab armis, L.: partem exercitūs ad bellum, L.: pubem in arcem obtinendam, L.—Fig., to call off, withdraw, remove: a rebus occultis philosophiam: ad Antiochum animo…

avolo.definition: ā-volō āvī, ātūrus, āre, to fly away: sublime: per umbras, Ct.—To flee, hasten away: nescio quo: hinc: citatis equis Romam, L.: iuvenis avolat ipse, V.—Fig., to flee away, vanish: voluptas avolat: me hinc avolaturum, …

avunculus.definition: avunculus ī, m dim. avus, a maternal uncle, mother's brother: tuus: eius, L.: magnus, a greatuncle.

avus.definition: avus ī, m 1 AV-, a grandfather: huius: maternus, L.—Of bees, a grandsire, V.—An ancestor, forefather: paternus, H.: avi atavique, V.
